q.q: Which is the best description of the internet?
o: The unique address of a web page
A program that reads and displays HTML
A global network of interconnected computers
A huge collection of websites and web pages
q.why: The internet is the hardware network; the WWW is the websites on it.

q.q: Who created the first website?
q.why: Tim Berners-Lee, a British computer scientist at CERN, made the first website.

q.q: What does a browser do with HTML tags?
o: Shows the tags on screen above the content
Sends the tags to the web server to check
Uses them to display the page, without showing the tags
Deletes the tags before saving the page
q.why: The tags are instructions for the browser, not content to display.

q.q: When did the first website go live?
q.why: The first website went live on 6 August 1991; 1989 is when the project started.

q.q: What is a URL?
o: A word or image you click to go to another page
The unique address of a web page
A program that displays web pages
q.why: A URL is the unique address of a web page, e.g. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news.

q.q: What is a hyperlink?
o: A program such as Chrome or Firefox
The unique address typed into the browser bar
A word or image you click to take you to another web page
A cable that joins computers together
q.why: A hyperlink is a word or image you click to go to another page.

q.q: Where was Tim Berners-Lee working when he made the first website?
o: CERN, a science laboratory in Switzerland
Google, a search company in California
Microsoft, a software company in the USA
The BBC, a broadcaster in London
q.why: He was working at CERN in Switzerland.

q.q: What did Tim Berners-Lee found in 1994?
q.why: In 1994 he founded the W3C, which sets web standards.

q.q: What do HTTP and HTML describe?
o: Both are names of early web browsers
HTTP is how pages are sent; HTML is how pages are written
Both describe how pages are styled with colours
HTTP is how pages are written; HTML is how pages are sent
q.why: He wrote the rules for HTTP (how pages are sent) and HTML (how pages are written).

q.q: Which of these uses the internet but is NOT part of the World Wide Web?
o: A page of videos on a website
q.why: Email and online gaming use the internet but are not part of the web.

q.q: How many colours should a good website colour scheme usually have?
q.why: A 3–5 colour scheme keeps a site clear and consistent.

q.q: Why is red text on a blue background a bad idea?
o: It makes the page load slowly
It is very hard to read
q.why: Poor contrast makes text difficult to read.

q.q: A small photo has been stretched to fill the page. What will it look like?
q.why: Enlarging a small bitmap makes it pixelated.

q.q: Which of these is good website design?
o: The same menu on every page
q.why: Consistent navigation is good design.

q.q: A large photo has been shrunk on the page using HTML only. What problem does this cause?
o: It is a huge, slow download
It turns into a GIF file
q.why: The full-size file is still downloaded, so it is slow; resize images properly before uploading.

q.q: Why is writing text inside an image a bad idea?
o: It always makes the image look pixelated
It always uses too many different fonts
It cannot be searched or read by screen readers
It stops the image from loading in Chrome
q.why: Text in an image can't be searched or read by screen readers; use real HTML text.

q.q: Why should a mouse-over change only the colour of a link, not make it bigger or bold?
o: Colour changes load more quickly than bold
Bigger text is not allowed in a navbar
Making it bigger or bold makes the layout jump
q.why: Bigger or bold text makes the layout jump, so change colour only.

q.q: A page is saved as 'new_page_1.htm'. What is the problem?
o: The number 1 means it uses the wrong colour scheme
It is not a real HTML file, so it won't open
It will only open in Chrome and not in Safari
Poor file naming; it should have a meaningful name
q.why: Give files meaningful names, e.g. hobbies.html.

q.q: Which font advice is good for a website?
o: Use one or two clear, web-safe fonts
Use Brush Script and Word Art for interest
Use a different font for every heading
Use as many fonts as the computer has
q.why: Too many fonts look messy and may not display; use one or two clear fonts.

q.q: Which is the best way to test your website's navigation?
o: Ask someone else, such as a younger sibling, to find a page
Check that every page uses five colours
Add a page counter to see how many visit
Make sure the music plays on every page
q.why: If someone else gets lost finding a page, your navigation needs work.

q.q: Why does a sunset photo saved as a GIF look grainy?
o: GIFs cannot be shown on websites
q.why: GIFs only have 256 colours, so photos look grainy; use JPEG for photos.

q.q: Why is navigation so important on a website?
o: It adds more colours to the site
Users will leave a website that is hard to navigate
It is required by law on every site
It makes the site load much faster
q.why: Research shows users simply leave sites that are hard to navigate.

q.q: Where should the main menu appear?
o: Only at the bottom of the last page
In a different place on each page
In the same place on every page
q.why: Consistency means the same menu on every page.

q.q: What is a rollover effect?
o: A page that scrolls down by itself slowly
A logo that spins round and round on the page
A button that changes when the mouse moves over it
A link that no longer goes to any page
q.why: Rollovers react to the mouse pointer, adding interactivity.

q.q: What is navigation?
o: How users move around a website
The code used to style a website
The colour scheme of a website
q.why: Navigation means how users move around a website.

q.q: What is a target audience?
o: The people who build the website
The number of visitors each day
The search engine that lists the site
The people the website is made for
q.why: The target audience is the people the site is made for.

q.q: Which is the best label for a button on a sports club website?
q.why: Label buttons with what the user gets, not clever names; nobody clicks a mystery button.

q.q: Where do most big websites put their logo or site name in the navigation bar?
o: In the centre of the page
At the bottom of the page
q.why: The logo or site name is at the left, often linking back to the home page.

q.q: Why do navigation bars highlight the current page or hovered link?
o: It shows the user where they are
It makes the page load faster
q.why: Highlighting the current or hovered link shows where you are.

q.q: What does HTML stand for?
q.why: HTML = HyperText Markup Language.

q.q: Which is a correct closing tag for a paragraph?
q.why: The closing tag puts a forward slash before the tag name.

q.q: What is the latest version of HTML?
q.why: The latest version is HTML5.

q.q: In <head><title>Hi</title></head>, which tag is nested inside which?
q.why: The title opens and closes inside the head.

q.q: What kind of file does your browser load when you visit a website?
o: A plain text file full of tags
q.why: Your browser loads a plain text file full of tags and draws the page from them.

q.q: What does HTML describe about a web page?
o: How it is sent across the internet
q.why: HTML describes the content and structure of a page.

q.q: What are attributes in HTML?
o: Extra information in the opening tag that changes how the tag looks or works
The text that is displayed between the opening and closing tags
Tags that are nested inside another tag
The forward slash that goes at the start of a closing tag
q.why: Tags can have attributes, which go inside the opening tag.

q.q: Which of these is correctly nested?
q.why: Close tags in the reverse order you opened them.

q.q: What is an HTML element?
o: Only the opening tag of a pair of tags
Any file whose name ends in .html
An opening tag, some content and a closing tag
The unique address of a web page
q.why: An element is an opening tag, some content, and a closing tag.

q.q: What brackets do HTML tags use?
q.why: Tags use angled brackets; CSS rules use curly brackets.

q.q: Which tag's content appears in the browser tab?
q.why: The title appears on the tab.

q.q: Where must all visible content go?
q.why: Only body content is displayed on the page.

q.q: What does <!DOCTYPE html> do?
o: Makes the largest heading on the page
Adds a link to another page
Tells the browser the document is HTML5
q.why: It declares the document type.

q.q: Which is the root element that every other tag goes inside?
q.why: <html> is the root element.

q.q: What does the <head> section hold?
o: All the visible text and images
All the headings that appear on the page
The links in the navigation bar
Meta information for the browser that doesn't appear on the page
q.why: <head> holds information the browser needs but that doesn't appear on the page itself.

q.q:
What does the

tag create?
o: A page title in the tab
A box to type a password
q.why: is a paragraph of text.

q.q: Why should you indent nested tags with the Tab key?
o: It changes the order of the tags
It makes the page text bigger
The browser will not work without it
It makes it clear which tags are inside which
q.why: Indenting makes it very clear what is inside what.

q.q: Lucy types her welcome message inside the <head> instead of the <body>. What happens?
o: It appears in the browser tab instead
It appears twice on the page as a heading
It appears in large bold text at the top
It will not appear properly on the page
q.why: Text typed into the head will not appear properly; visible content goes in the body.

q.q: In the head and body comparison with a person, what is the body?
o: The name shown in the tab
q.why: The head holds information you can't see; the body is what everyone sees.

q.q: In a basic page, which correct order do these tags open in?
q.why: html is the root; head (with title) comes before body.

q.q: Which tag makes a bullet-point list?
q.why: <ul> = unordered (bulleted) list; <ol> is numbered.

q.q: What does the alt attribute of an image do?
o: Adds a border around the image
Says where the image file is saved
Sets the width and height of the image in pixels
Gives text shown if the image is missing, read by screen readers
q.why: alt = alternative text, shown if the image cannot be found and read aloud by screen readers.

q.q: Why is called a self-closing tag?
o: It has no content between tags, so it has no closing tag
It must be the last tag on the page
It closes the browser when clicked
q.why: It uses attributes but has no content, so there is no closing tag.

q.q: Which heading tag gives the biggest heading?
q.why: <h1> is the largest heading, down to <h6>.

q.q: What does the src attribute of an image tell the browser?
o: What text to show if the image is missing
How wide the image should be
What happens when the image is clicked
Where the image file is saved
q.why: src is the source: where the image file is saved.

q.q: Which tag makes a numbered list?
q.why: <ol> is an ordered (numbered) list.

q.q: What does <li> stand for?
q.why: <li> means list item; each item in an <ol> or <ul> goes in its own <li>.

q.q: In what units do the width and height attributes of an image set its size?
q.why: width and height set the size of the image on screen in pixels.

q.q: Why might copying HTML from Word break an image or link?
o: Word deletes all the closing tags
Word turns straight quotes into curly quotes
Word changes the image to a GIF
q.why: Browsers don't understand curly quotes in attributes.

q.q: Which is a correctly written image tag?
q.why: is self-closing and uses src and alt attributes in straight quotes.

q.q: You want a list of your top three teams ranked 1, 2, 3. Which structure should you use?
q.why: A numbered list is an <ol> with an <li> for each item.

q.q: Which attribute gives a link's destination?
q.why: href = hypertext reference, the destination.

q.q: Index.html and Hobbies.html are in the same folder. Which href links to Hobbies?
q.why: Same folder: just the file name.

q.q: contact.html is in a folder called Contact inside MyWebsite. Which href links to it from Index.html?
q.why: Folder name, slash, file name.

q.q: Which file is the home page of a website?
q.why: Index.html is universally treated as the first page and web servers open it automatically.

q.q: Which tag is used to make a hyperlink?
q.why: Links use the anchor tag, <a>, with an href attribute.

q.q: In Click Here, what does the user see and click?
q.why: The text between the tags is what you see and click; href is not displayed.

q.q: What does ../ at the start of a link mean?
o: Open the link in a new tab
q.why: Two dots mean 'go up one folder'.

q.q: Why should you avoid image paths like C:/myimage.jpg?
o: They only work on your own computer and break once the site is uploaded
They turn the image into a GIF
They make the image download more slowly
q.why: Use relative paths like images/logo.jpg so the site works once uploaded.

q.q: Which of these is an absolute link?
q.why: An absolute link is a full address, used for a different site.

q.q: A pupil's link to Hobbies.html doesn't work. The file is actually called Hobbies.html.txt. What went wrong?
o: The file should be in a separate subfolder
The file was saved as a text file, not an HTML file
The link should use the src attribute
The href needs to include C:/ at the start
q.why: Check that files really end in .html, not .html.txt.

q.q: What is the div tag used for?
o: Displaying an image on the page
A container that groups elements into a section
q.why: div = division, a container.

q.q: To build a navbar, which tags do we put inside a div?
q.why: The hyperlinks (<a> tags) are nested inside the div.

q.q: Why copy the same navbar to every page?
o: Browsers require it on every page
To hide the links from search engines
q.why: Consistent menus are key to good navigation.

q.q: What does div stand for?
q.why: div is short for division.

q.q: What does a div look like on the page on its own?
o: It shows a grey menu bar across the top
It shows the word 'div' above the contents
It draws a thick black border round its contents
It does not look like anything until it is styled
q.why: On its own it doesn't look like anything, but it lets you group and style things together.

q.q: Where does the closing go when building a navbar?
o: At the very end of the head
q.why: The div opens before the first link and closes after the last one.

q.q: Which HTML5 tag is made specially for navigation bars?
q.why: HTML5 has a <nav> tag that tells browsers and screen readers 'this is the menu'.

q.q: What should you do after building your navbar?
q.why: Test every link after building the navbar.

q.q: Which styling method is recommended for large websites?
q.why: One .css file styles every page.

q.q: Where does the <link> tag for a style sheet go?
q.why: Style and link tags go in the head.

q.q: Which tag connects an HTML page to an external CSS file?
q.why: <link rel="stylesheet" href="..."> connects the page to a .css file.

q.q: What does CSS stand for?
q.why: CSS = Cascading Style Sheets.

q.q: What is inline styling?
o: A style attribute on one tag
q.why: Inline styling puts a style attribute on one tag.

q.q: Why is inline styling one of the worst ways to style a large site?
o: You would have to repeat it on every tag on every page
It can only change the font, not colours
It must be saved as a separate file
q.why: Inline styling must be repeated everywhere; only use it for small one-off changes.

q.q: A <style> tag in the head contains h1 { color: green; }. Which headings turn green?
o: Only the first <h1> on the page
All <h1> tags on every page of the site
q.why: The style applies to all <h1> tags on that page, but not other pages.

q.q: What is the main advantage of an external style sheet?
o: It is written inside the body
Change one line and every linked page updates
It only styles one tag at a time
It needs no link from the HTML page
q.why: Change one line in the .css file and every linked page updates.

q.q: A page links to myFancyStylesheet.css with href="myFancyStylesheet.css" but no styling appears. What is the most likely problem?
o: The link tag is inside the head
The CSS file is not in the same folder as the HTML page
The CSS file is saved with a .css extension
The CSS rules use curly brackets
q.why: With just a file name, the .css must be in the same folder, or you must give the path.

q.q: What file extension should an external style sheet be saved with?
q.why: It is saved as a .css file, not .txt.

q.q: A small site has one page that needs special styling used nowhere else. Which method suits best?
o: Word Art pasted into the page
A separate external style sheet for every tag
An inline style on every tag
A <style> tag in that page's head
q.why: A <style> tag suits small sites or styling used on only one page.

q.q: Which CSS rule styles every <h2> on the page?
q.why: A tag selector is just the tag name.

q.q: How do you style both h1 and h2 with one rule?
q.why: Separate selectors with a comma.

q.q: Which selector targets elements with class="house"?
q.why: Class selectors start with a full stop.

q.q: Which line correctly makes text red?
q.why: Property, colon, value, semicolon; American spelling.

q.q: What is a CSS selector?
o: The semicolon at the end of each property
The tag that links a style sheet to a page
The value given to a property, such as red
The part of a CSS rule that chooses which tags to style
q.why: A selector chooses which elements a CSS rule styles.

q.q: Ben writes colour: blue; in his CSS. What happens?
o: The text turns black and bold
q.why: CSS uses American spelling: color. The browser ignores colour.

q.q: What must end each property: value pair in CSS?
q.why: Each property and value ends in a semicolon; colons go between property and value.

q.q: What goes inside the curly brackets of a CSS rule?
q.why: After the selector come curly brackets holding the properties and values.

q.q: The CSS has .house { color: white; }. Which HTML element turns white?
o: I am in the blue house.
I am in the blue house.
q.why: A class selector styles only elements with class="house".

q.q: Suddenly every rule after the h1 rule in your CSS stops working. What should you check first?
o: The spelling of the page title
A missing semicolon or curly bracket
The order of the links in the navbar
q.why: If styling suddenly breaks, check your punctuation first.

q.q: Which rule gives every <h1> and <h2> the Arial font?
q.why: List selectors with a comma, then property: value; inside curly brackets.
